body:
### Describe the bug

`Cython.Build.Dependencies.parse_dependencies` does not record a `.pxd` dependency when a submodule is cimported with the single-line form `from pkg cimport submodule`. Only `pkg` is recorded, not `pkg.submodule`, so `cythonize` treats dependent modules as up to date after `pkg/submodule.pxd` changes and reuses stale generated code.

The cause is `dependency_after_from_regex`, which collects the names after `cimport`. Both alternatives are anchored with `^` under `re.MULTILINE`, so they only match at the start of a line. A name on the same line as `from ... cimport` is never matched; the search skips ahead to the next indented line, if any.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```python
import re

# Verbatim from Cython/Build/Dependencies.py
dependency_regex = re.compile(
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]* from     [ \t\f]+ cython\.cimports\.([\w.]+) [ \t\f]+ c?import ) |"
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]* from     [ \t\f]+ ([\w.]+) [ \t\f]+ cimport ) |"
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]* c?import [ \t\f]+ cython\.cimports\.([\w.]+) ) |"
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]* cimport  [ \t\f]+ ([\w.]+ (?:[ \t\f]* , [ \t\f]* [\w.]+)*) ) |"
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]* cdef     [ \t\f]+ extern [ \t\f]+ from [ \t\f]+ ['\"] ([^'\"]+) ['\"] ) |"
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]* include  [ \t\f]+ ['\"] ([^'\"]+) ['\"] )",
    re.MULTILINE | re.VERBOSE)
dependency_after_from_regex = re.compile(
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]+ \( ([\w., \t\f]*) \) [ \t\f]* [#\n]) |"
    r"(?:^ [ \t\f]+    ([\w., \t\f]*)    [ \t\f]* [#\n])",
    re.MULTILINE | re.VERBOSE)

# Same logic as the cimport branch of parse_dependencies()
def collect_cimports(source):
    source = source.replace('\\\n', ' ').replace('\t', ' ')
    cimports = []
    for m in dependency_regex.finditer(source):
        _, cimport_from, _, cimport_list, _, _ = m.groups()
        if cimport_from:
            cimports.append(cimport_from)
            m2 = dependency_after_from_regex.search(source, pos=m.end())
            if m2:
                multiline, one_line = m2.groups()
                subimports = multiline or one_line
                cimports.extend("{}.{}".format(cimport_from, s.strip())
                                for s in subimports.split(","))
        elif cimport_list:
            cimports.extend(x.strip() for x in cimport_list.split(","))
    return cimports

print(collect_cimports("from pkg.submodule cimport sym\n"))
# ['pkg.submodule']   -> pkg/submodule.pxd is tracked

print(collect_cimports("from pkg cimport submodule\n"))
# ['pkg']             -> pkg/submodule.pxd is NOT tracked
```

In Cython source terms:

```cython
# consumer.pxd
from pkg cimport submodule              # pkg/submodule.pxd not tracked
from pkg.submodule cimport some_symbol  # pkg/submodule.pxd tracked
```

### Expected behaviour

Both forms depend on `pkg/submodule.pxd`, so `parse_dependencies` should record `pkg.submodule` in both cases.

### OS

Linux (x86_64, riscv64)

### Python version

3.13

### Cython version

3.3.0 (the regex is unchanged on current master)

### Additional context

We hit this as a stale-cache failure. A `.pxd` changed some functions to `cpdef inline`, which changed the C functions exported through `__pyx_capi__`. Consumer modules that used `from pkg cimport submodule` were not recompiled and failed at import with `ImportError: ... does not export expected C function ...`.

Writing the cimport as `from pkg.submodule cimport ...` avoids the problem.

comment_data.body: I have a fix with tests for this, happy to open a PR unless you are already on it.

title: [BUG] parse_dependencies misses .pxd dependency for single-line 'from pkg cimport submodule'
